The hilarious, instantly recognizable “Whassup!” sequence in Scary Movie was a direct parody of the wildly popular Budweiser commercial campaign titled “True” that dominated television in late 1999 and 2000. By perfectly mashing up the terrifying, tension-filled opening phone call from Scream with the inescapable beer advertisement, the Wayans brothers created one of the defining comedic pop-culture moments of the decade. However, to ensure the joke landed without getting sued by Anheuser-Busch, the art department made a very subtle visual tweak: during the escalating, tongue-wagging shouting match between the killer, Shorty, and his friends, the beer can Ghostface is holding doesn’t say “Budweiser”—the label actually reads “Killer.”

Scary Movie (2000), directed by Keenen Ivory Wayans, starring Anna Faris, Marlon Wayans, Shawn Wayans, Regina Hall, Shannon Elizabeth. A group of bumbling, highly oblivious teenagers are stalked by a masked killer seeking revenge exactly one year after they accidentally covered up a car crash, loudly spoofing the biggest teen slasher films and pop culture trends of the era.
